questions.question: In 1887, whose work did Heinrich Rudolf Hertz apply to conduct a series of experiments from which he generated radio waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Clerk Maxwell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell** was a Scottish physicist who formulated a set of equations that describe the behavior of **electric and magnetic fields**, known as Maxwell's equations.
 
• Maxwell’s equations predicted the existence of **electromagnetic waves**, which could travel through space at the speed of light.
 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz** applied Maxwell’s theoretical work in 1887 to conduct experiments that demonstrated the existence of **radio waves**.
 
• Hertz’s experiments involved the generation of electromagnetic waves, confirming Maxwell’s prediction and laying the foundation for the development of **wireless communication technologies**.
 
• Maxwell’s contributions are considered a cornerstone of modern physics, as his equations unified the fields of **electricity, magnetism, and light.**
 
• The confirmation of Maxwell's theory by Hertz eventually led to the invention of the **radio, television, and radar systems**.
 
• Maxwell’s work is a significant milestone in the development of the field of **electromagnetic theory**, influencing various scientific and technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Christiaan Huygens**__

 __
 
• **Christiaan Huygens** was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, and astronomer known for his work on the **wave theory of light**.
 
• He proposed the **Huygens-Fresnel principle**, which describes how wavefronts propagate.
 
• Huygens invented the **pendulum clock**, significantly improving timekeeping accuracy.
 
• While his work on waves was influential, it primarily focused on **light**, not the electromagnetic waves described by Maxwell.
 
 
 
• **Christian Doppler**__
 __
 
• **Christian Doppler** was an Austrian physicist best known for the **Doppler effect**, which describes the change in frequency or wavelength of a wave in relation to an observer moving relative to the source of the wave.
 
• The Doppler effect has applications in **astronomy, weather radar, and medical imaging** (e.g., Doppler ultrasound).
 
• His work is unrelated to the generation or propagation of **radio waves**.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Young**__
 
 
• **Thomas Young** was an English polymath known for his contributions to the **double-slit experiment**, which demonstrated the wave nature of light.
 
• He also made significant contributions to the fields of **vision, elasticity, and linguistics.**
 
• Young’s work focused on **optics and mechanics**, not electromagnetic waves or radio wave generation.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is a Pteridophyte which is usually found in moist, shady places or gardens and on hills where the temperatures are low?

__
 
• **Ferns** are classified as **Pteridophytes**, which are vascular plants that reproduce via spores rather than seeds.
 
• They thrive in **moist and shady environments**, making them common in gardens, forests, and areas with high humidity.
 
• These plants are often found on **hills** or in regions with **low temperatures**, which provide the ideal conditions for their growth.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B can do it in 24 days. If they do the work alternately, in how many days will they finish the work, provided that A begins the work?

Total Work = LCM(15, 24) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 units/day, Efficiency of B = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day.

Work done in the first 2 days (A + B) = 8 + 5 = 13 units.

Work done in 18 days (9 alternating pairs) = 13 × 9 = 117 units.

Remaining 3 units are done by A on the 19th day in 3/8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 ³/₈ days.**

questions.question: When 7516, 7635 and 7992 are divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case is the same. The product of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number leaving the same remainder is the HCF of their absolute differences.

Differences = (7635 − 7516), (7992 − 7635), (7992 − 7516) = 119, 357, 476.

x = HCF(119, 357, 476) = 119.

Product of digits of x = 1 × 1 × 9 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 7516, 7635, and 7992.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number x that divides given numbers a, b, and c leaving the same remainder is given by x = HCF(|a − b|, |b − c|, |c − a|).

**Calculations:**

⇒ |a − b| = 7635 − 7516 = 119

⇒ |b − c| = 7992 − 7635 = 357

⇒ |c − a| = 7992 − 7516 = 476

⇒ x = HCF(119, 357, 476)

⇒ We can observe that 357 = 119 × 3 and 476 = 119 × 4.

⇒ Hence, the HCF of 119, 357, and 476 is 119, meaning x = 119.

⇒ We need the product of the digits of x.

⇒ Product of digits = 1 × 1 × 9 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Numbers with Different Remainders

When finding the greatest number dividing a, b, c and leaving remainders r₁, r₂, r₃ respectively, the required number is HCF(a − r₁, b − r₂, c − r₃).

LCM of Numbers Leaving the Same Remainder

To find the smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case, the number is LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Difference Property of HCF

The HCF of any set of numbers is always a factor of their absolute differences. This property simplifies finding the HCF of large numbers by focusing on evaluating the smallest difference between them.
</p

questions.question: The greatest number that will divide 42, 84 and 153 so as to leave the same remainder in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the greatest number that leaves the same remainder, take the HCF of their absolute differences.

Differences: |84 − 42| = 42, |153 − 84| = 69, |153 − 42| = 111.

Required number = HCF of (42, 69, 111).

HCF(3 × 14, 3 × 23, 3 × 37) = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 42, 84 and 153.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case is given by the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z| and |z − x|.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First difference = |84 − 42| = 42

⇒ Second difference = |153 − 84| = 69

⇒ Third difference = |153 − 42| = 111

⇒ Now, we need to find the HCF of 42, 69, and 111.

⇒ Prime factorization of 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 69 = 3 × 23

⇒ Prime factorization of 111 = 3 × 37

⇒ The common factor among all three numbers is 3.

⇒ HCF(42, 69, 111) = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest number leaving same unknown remainder

When a number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder, the required greatest number is the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Greatest number leaving specific remainders

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively is the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Least number leaving same remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is given by LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Least number leaving different remainders

If divided by x, y, z leaving remainders a, b, c where (x − a) = (y − b) = (z − c) = k, the required number is LCM(x, y, z) − k.

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 75%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 47% only?

Let the initial expenditure and price base be 100 units.

If consumption remains unchanged, the new expenditure after a 75% price hike will be 175.

Required reduction on the new price base = 175 − 147 = 28.

Percentage reduction in consumption = (28 ÷ 175) × 100 = 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10,000
